model_annotation: The image displays two side-by-side line charts comparing the IWF Fiskalindex (left y-axis) and the debt-to-GDP ratio (Schuldenquote, right y-axis) over time for two different entities: “Gesamtstaat” (overall state) in the left chart and “Zentralstaat” (central state) in the right chart, both spanning from 1995 to 2020. In the left chart, the IWF Fiskalindex (blue line with circle markers) begins near 0 in 1995, rises to a peak of approximately 1.0 around 2008, then declines to about 0.2 by 2018 before rising slightly to 0.5 in 2020. The purple line with triangle markers, representing the IWF Fiskalindex for the overall state, starts near 0, rises gradually to about 0.4 by 2005, then climbs sharply to 2.0 by 2020. The right y-axis, labeled “Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat,” shows the overall state’s debt-to-GDP ratio (blue triangles) starting near 80 in 1995, peaking around 115 in 2010–2015, then slightly declining to 110 by 2020. In the right chart, the IWF Fiskalindex for the central state (blue line with circle markers) starts near 0 in 1995, rises to 1.0 by 2008, drops to 0.0 in 2010, then rises again to 0.6 by 2020. The purple line with triangle markers for the central state’s IWF Fiskalindex begins near 0, rises to 0.3 by 2005, then climbs steeply to 2.0 by 2020. The right y-axis, labeled “Schuldenquote Zentralstaat,” shows the central state’s debt-to-GDP ratio (blue triangles) starting near 50 in 1995, peaking around 70 in 2010, then declining to 40 by 2018 before rising to 50 by 2020. Both charts use a linear x-axis from 1995 to 2020 with 5-year intervals, and gridlines are present for both axes.
